name: National Democracy
summary: National Democracy is the Philippine Marxist-Leninist-Maoist doctrine that the country is semi-colonial and semi-feudal, ruled by US imperialism, big compradors and landlords. It calls for a people's democratic revolution through protracted people's war led by the Communist Party and an army in the countryside, then a people's democratic republic with genuine land reform, state-led national industrialisation and a coalition government, with socialism as a later stage.
scope: The national democratic line of the Communist Party of the Philippines and the National Democratic Front, as set out in Sison's Philippine Society and Revolution (1970), the CPP's 1968 program and the NDFP's 12-point program. It does not cover other uses of the term national democracy, such as the Polish Endecja, and the legal party-list organisations are treated as part of the same movement. Many social questions are not addressed in the sources and are answered with low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Full list of the twelve program points, including minorities, women, independent foreign policy and people's war.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Part of the "comprehensive and progressive social policy" in point 8 of the NDFP program, with free social services under the people's democratic state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Defence of workers' wages and living standards is a standing demand of the movement's labour front; the program commits to a progressive social policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The program aims at an independent, self-reliant economy built through national industrialisation and state-led planning, and opposes the dominance of imperialist capital and big compradors over markets.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1968 program puts major raw-material, energy and heavy and basic industries in the hands of the state sector.

unions-good.rationale: The working class leads the revolution in the program, and legal labour organisations are a core part of the national democratic mass movement.

property-fundamental.rationale: Landlord and comprador property is to be expropriated, though patriotic private enterprise and national-bourgeois property are protected, so private property is not treated as a fundamental inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The program calls for ending the dominance of foreign monopoly capital and compradors, and for state control of the commanding heights.

cut-welfare.rationale: A progressive social policy is a program plank, and adherents see welfare cuts as part of imperialist neoliberal policy.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The program does not address drugs; adherents are split between decriminalisation and condemnation of the drug trade.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed; the program promises freedom of speech but also state control of mass media.

strong-leader.rationale: Leadership is by the party and democratic centralism, not a personal strongman, and adherents condemned Marcos-style one-man rule.

state-harmful.rationale: The program builds a people's democratic state with its own army and organs of power, so the state is essential to it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.

reviewHistory.rationale: The existing police and army are described as instruments of the ruling classes and US imperialism, which the revolution aims to defeat.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is not about military spending, which this statement now asks about alone.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: The program stresses democratic centralism with elected bodies at each level plus autonomy for minorities, so neither localism nor centralism clearly wins.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not in the program; adherents are divided between women's rights groups' support and a Catholic-influenced caution among allied religious sectors.

more-religion-public.rationale: The 1968 program targets church influence in culture and education, though it guarantees freedom of belief.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The program calls for a national, scientific and mass culture, and condemns imperialist and feudal culture.

gradual-change.rationale: The program calls armed revolution the only road and rejects the parliamentary road as revisionist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not a theme; the movement is nationalist but internationalist toward workers, and the Philippines is a country of emigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 1968 program opposes the UN, ASEAN and SEATO as tools of imperialism.

free-trade.rationale: Opposes imperialist domination of trade and calls for an independent, self-reliant economy.

nation-first.rationale: National sovereignty against US imperialism is central, but the movement also stresses proletarian internationalism and an independent, peaceful foreign policy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Opposed to imperialist military intervention, which it sees as a pretext for domination; the program calls for an independent and peaceful foreign policy.

limit-growth.rationale: The program wants industrialisation and rising production, though it adds agricultural sustainability.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The program stresses modernisation of agriculture and industry but puts social revolution first, not technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Armed people's war to overthrow the system is the first point of the NDFP program.

experts-over-public.rationale: The mass line holds that the masses are the makers of history; nothing explicit on experts.

central-planning.rationale: The state sector would hold basic industry in a planned national industrialisation, but private and cooperative sectors continue in the democratic stage.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state sector owns key industries and drives national industrialisation.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Free land distribution to peasants and support for patriotic small and medium business, against landlord and comprador concentration.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolition belongs to the far communist stage; the national democratic stage keeps wage labour and a private sector.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Movement favours class struggle and independent unions rather than state-recognised bodies setting wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: The CPP leads the revolution, but the stated aim is a coalition government of several classes and parties in a people's democratic republic.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The program calls for a people's democratic republic and the movement attacks feudalism.

democracy-best.rationale: It claims a people's democracy as superior and rejects bourgeois parliaments, so it answers neither for liberal democracy nor against democracy as such.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power is to rest on a coalition government of four classes and elected bodies, not workers' councils alone.

natural-rulers.rationale: Opposes feudal hierarchy and the rule of landlord and comprador elites.

political-violence-never.rationale: Armed struggle is the principal form of revolutionary struggle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing stated; the movement values the revolutionary war for political ends and opposes imperialist wars.

separate-church-state.rationale: Freedom of religion is promised while the church-state union of colonial times is condemned as a tool of domination.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Advocates a scientific culture and secular democratic state.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state organises defence and justice through the people's army and people's courts.

military-superiority.rationale: The movement is hostile to the existing military and to arms races, and favours a peaceful foreign policy, though it builds its own army.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The program defends the rights of minorities such as the Moro and Cordillera peoples within a multi-ethnic nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Sison's analysis rests on Mao's view that class contradictions drive the replacement of old societies by new ones.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The program supports minorities' land claims and the self-determination of the Cordillera and other indigenous peoples.

civilizational-union.rationale: Movement is nationalist and class-based, not civilizational.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Opposes capitalist profit-seeking and calls for production for the people.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The program promises democratic rights and does not rank duties first.

limit-population.rationale: Marxist-Leninist tradition blames poverty on social structure, not population.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The program seeks national industrialisation as a goal.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources contain no position on encryption; a movement itself under state surveillance might favour it, but nothing is stated, so it stays neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: Committed to revolutionary transformation of society toward a new democratic order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Strongly ideological, grounding itself in Marxism-Leninism-Maoism, though it values practice and "seeking truth from facts".

direct-action.rationale: Armed struggle is principal and legal struggle "essential but secondary", which includes parliamentary participation by legal fronts.

means-match-ends.rationale: Treats violent means as necessary for a democratic end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Seeks industrialisation, not a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A communist-stage aim, not part of the democratic stage.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Long-term socialist and communist goal, but the program's current stage is not about this.

production-for-use.rationale: Orients the economy to national industrialisation and people's needs over foreign profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist analysis of landlords and capital as exploiters is central, but patriotic private business is accepted.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The democratic stage is a joint dictatorship of the people's classes, with the working class leading, not a pure proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: The program starts with free land distribution and mutual aid teams, then cooperatives, and only efficient plantations become state farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Describes imperialism as the number one enemy of peoples and a cause of aggression, in Leninist terms.

taxation-theft.rationale: Opposite of the state-building position of the program.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Emphasises class, national and collective rights such as those of national minorities.

state-as-business.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.

reviewHistory.rationale: The program makes the state an instrument of the people's classes with a state economic sector, which is the opposite of treating citizens as customers.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value turns on whether citizens are customers who can leave, and the statement now asks only whether government should be run on business principles.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

positive-liberty.rationale: Land and social policy are meant to give material means; the program links rights to material liberation.

media-academia-power.rationale: Treats imperialist-dominated mass media as tools of subservience, but not as exceeding state power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Rejects racism; its anti-colonial analysis blames US domination.

organic-representation.rationale: Uses elected representation within democratic centralism, but also includes sectoral organisations in the front.

total-state.rationale: The 1968 program has state control of education and media, but within a mixed economy with private and cooperative sectors.

national-rebirth.rationale: Frames its revolution as a national renewal against colonial domination; not as decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The movement defines imperialism, including US expansion, as the main enemy, and its program seeks national independence rather than expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The program attacks feudalism and landlord rule over peasants, which is the system of personal dependency this statement describes.

bound-labor.rationale: Opposes feudal exploitation and calls for land to the tiller.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Neither the program nor Sison's text takes up the philosophy of knowledge in these terms; Maoist stress on class standpoint cuts both ways, so it is left neutral.

single-common-good.rationale: Class analysis denies a single common good in a class-divided society.

revive-national-language.rationale: The 1968 program calls for promoting a national language in education and culture, which supports reviving national language use, though no revival of a lapsed one is discussed.

school-vouchers.rationale: The program calls for free education run under state control.

economic-freedom.rationale: The program rejects the liberal doctrine that markets come first, pursuing state-led national industrialisation and land reform ahead of economic liberalism.

rule-by-example.rationale: The program rests on organisation, democratic centralism and law-like discipline, not on the moral example of rulers alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: National liberation from imperialism and the self-determination of minorities are central points.

force-without-un.rationale: The movement rejects imperialist intervention and the UN as an instrument, but sees force as justified for liberation, not for a state abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Promotes a scientific culture, though it allies with religious progressives.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class struggle between peasants and workers and landlords and compradors is the foundation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Calls for a national culture drawing on the people's heritage, and critiques only imperialist and feudal elements.

dominated-front.rationale: The program calls for joint action with other oppressed peoples and anti-imperialist forces.

workers-nation.rationale: Combines national struggle with proletarian internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Pledges revolutionary emancipation of women in all spheres.

ban-interest.rationale: Opposes usury in the countryside; not interest generally.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Sison condemns colonial racial and Christian chauvinism against Muslims and mountain peoples, and the program defends the democratic rights of national minorities.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Leninist view that the existing state serves landlords and compradors underpins the program.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Supports minority cultures but doesn't treat immigration.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory not part of its class analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Denounces bureaucrat capitalism and corruption as a core problem.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Nothing in the program supports eugenic controls, and the program's people-centred, anti-discrimination social policy runs against them.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Condemns abuses by the state security forces as a core grievance.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program gives the state major economic roles, with industry, energy and education under state control, so a minimal state is the opposite of its aim.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The movement's anti-colonial analysis condemns racism, and nothing in its documents supports discouraging mixed marriages.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Democratic rights and minorities' rights are program points, though it does not use universalist language.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Maoism accepts socialism in one country but also supports world revolution.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The 1968 program promises freedom of religion and belief, which excludes legal limits on conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No part of the program touches food-animal law, and the movement has no religious basis for such a ban, so it disagrees.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The 1968 program targets church influence in schools and calls for state control of education, so religious instruction in state schools would be unwelcome.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Maoist line favours a strong people's state against hostile powers.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Claims legitimacy through the people but through revolution rather than consent procedures.

trade-surplus.rationale: The program seeks national industrialisation and independent economy but does not discuss export surpluses, so it is neutral.

population-transfer.rationale: Opposes ethnic cleansing; supports minority rights.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Armed overthrow of the existing state is point one of the NDFP program, which is directly opposed to a pacifist principle on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Class struggle is the driver, not individual competition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Domination by imperialism and landlords is the central evil, though not in that vocabulary.

separated-powers.rationale: Democratic centralism rather than checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: The program makes the CPP the leader of revolution.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Workers and peasants are the main force, and policies favour them.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The program makes the working class the leading revolutionary force and the NDF's mass movement supports labour organising, so restrictions on strikes are opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Blames imperialism and feudalism, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The program upholds the rights and self-determination of minorities as part of national unity, rather than seeing diversity as a weakness.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The program's model is elected representative bodies at each level, not selection by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The movement's own account of the Marcos martial-law years is of repression of dissenters, so it rejects emergency suspension of protections as a tool against opponents.

party-controls-media.rationale: The program wants state control of mass media, but a coalition government with multiple parties.

party-commands-army.rationale: The 1968 program holds that the people's army is built and led by the party, a central point of Maoist military doctrine.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The program and constitution organise the party on democratic centralism, under which adopted decisions bind all members.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Opposes supranational structures as imperialist tools.

clerical-rule.rationale: The program's secular democratic republic leaves no place for senior clergy as the highest authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Leninist defeatism applies to inter-imperialist war; the Philippines is not a great power.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Calls for ending unequal relations and treaties with the US and opposes SEATO.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No housing tenure policy is stated in the documents, so no position can be given.

people-in-arms.rationale: Builds a people's army and wider people's defence system, but also a regular army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural base areas matter strategically, but no moral claim in the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement recruited heavily from students and intellectuals; mixed.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Defends national and minority cultures against imperialist cultural domination.

death-penalty.rationale: The movement opposes the state's death penalty in practice but does not state a doctrine.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The program calls for a national, scientific and mass culture and state control of education, so teaching creationism is unwelcome.

minority-language-support.rationale: Upholds the rights of national minorities and a national mass culture.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Opposes imperialist debt domination as part of ending unequal relations.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Formal independence is called "semi-colonial", and the revolution must change the economic base.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The program envisages a people's democratic republic, not a procedure of constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The program promises rights while qualifying them in revolutionary conditions.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Favours self-reliance and rejects imperialist aid with strings.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The program proposes a people's democratic republic with elected bodies at each level but does not say how the head of state is chosen.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Landlord and comprador property is to be taken for the people while patriotic private property stays, which treats property as conditional on national benefit.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Sison attacks Soviet revisionism after 1956, but the movement's sources do not call the USSR state-capitalist as a thesis, and it credits earlier Soviet socialism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environment is mentioned only as agricultural sustainability; no stand on regulatory principles.

collective-defense.rationale: The 1968 program opposes SEATO and US-led military pacts as instruments of imperialism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The program targets church influence in schools and culture but also guarantees freedom of religion and the movement allies with progressive clergy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A republican, anti-feudal and materialist program rejects sacral rule.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The movement supports minorities' self-determination, so it would not endorse force against secession, though it also seeks national unity against imperialism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: Autonomy for the Moro and Cordillera peoples is a program point, which is the nearest analogue.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

leader-cult.rationale: Sison and Mao are honoured in party literature, but the program does not call for a national leader cult.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Maoist line from which the CPP comes holds that class struggle continues under socialism and that the CPP's rectification campaigns fight revisionism.

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1968 program calls for free distribution of land to landless peasants and ending feudal landlordism, calling land the central issue of the revolution.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Anti-expansionist and anti-imperialist in outlook, and not framed in ethnic nationality terms.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The program guarantees freedom of thought and religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Pledges emancipation of women in all spheres and guarantees freedom of belief.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement is national-territorial and class-based, not based on kinship across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Supports the self-determination and democratic rights of Moro, Cordillera and other minorities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist materialism is a basic premise, though Maoism also stresses consciousness and the mass line.

ban-cartels.rationale: The program opposes foreign monopoly capital and compradors, but states no competition-law position.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The program seeks a self-reliant economy but plans peaceful foreign relations and trade, not a closed bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: Maoist tradition favours moral incentives, but the CPP program does not state it for the democratic stage.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The CPP's view is that a party-led army builds rural bases and creates conditions, in Sison's words the problem is no longer how to start a revolution, though it stresses mass base-building rather than foco.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: It attacks feudal landlord privilege and calls for a people's democratic republic.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sison condemns colonial rule, including US colonial education and "benevolent assimilation", as domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: Calls for a national language and national, scientific education, and opposes subservient colonial schooling.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Leninist analysis in Sison's work holds that imperialism is moribund and in permanent crisis.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Seeking influence in former imperial territories contradicts the movement's opposition to imperialism and unequal relations among nations.

delink-world-market.rationale: Seeks self-reliant national industrialisation and an end to unequal relations but not full autarky.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The program upholds the people's democratic rights, which sit against allowing private owners to discriminate freely.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The program promises democratic rights but rejects bourgeois constitutionalism as such.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Calls for terminating unequal treaties with the US; colonial-era division of peoples is not mentioned.

elective-rulers.rationale: The program calls for elected representative bodies in a people's democratic republic.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism subordinates the minority to the majority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The revolution is justified as resistance to a ruling system seen as illegitimate and oppressive.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rejects the existing parliament as a ruling-class tool but proposes elected people's congresses.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rejects charity as a substitute for structural change and land reform.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Calls for active participation in revolution.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Sison describes US-style schooling and media as making Filipinos politically subservient and boosting demand for American goods.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Sison's text says colonial control used church, schools and media as well as force, a point close to hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The core analysis is that the Philippine economy is semi-colonial, with foreign monopoly capital and compradors extracting from it.

party-own-road.rationale: The CPP broke with the Soviet-line party and its program calls the Philippines' revolution its own road, though it admires China.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Calls for an independent, self-reliant economy and opposes imperialist loans and investment.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Supports indigenous self-determination but not leadership over others.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Opposes fascist-type rule, which Sison predicts of the ruling class, though no constitutional proposal is stated.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: A communist movement that rejects equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not a topic in its sources; materialist outlook inclines against.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Women's emancipation is a program point; male disadvantage is not.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: National-democratic path is adapted to national conditions, but not framed as civilization.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Sees the existing armed forces as tools of reactionary classes and US imperialism.

office-by-exam.rationale: Program uses elected bodies, not examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The program breaks foreign capital's dominance and supports nationalisation of key sectors.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Elected representative bodies within democratic centralism are accountable to those who elected them.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land goes free to those who till it, which differs from community tenure at use only.

single-official-language.rationale: Promotes a national language but defends minority rights.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The program breaks foreign monopoly control of the economy, which includes foreign land and plantations.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Opposes imperialist interference, though it supports liberation wars in solidarity.

corporate-influence.rationale: Attacks comprador and monopoly capital's control of politics and state.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Opposes great-power domination of other countries.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The program rejects the existing legal order as that of ruling classes but demands discipline under its own organs, so its stance on a general duty is unstated.

non-intervention.rationale: Calls for an independent, peaceful foreign policy and rejects imperialist interference.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The movement's analysis blames imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat capitalism, not a secret minority conspiracy.

local-production.rationale: Seeks rural industrialisation and self-reliance but not localism for its own sake.

informal-organisation.rationale: Insists on disciplined party organisation and democratic centralism.

national-law-over-international.rationale: National sovereignty is central though no stand on courts.

religious-nation.rationale: National unity is based on class and anti-imperialism; Moro and Christians alike are part of it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Rejects deference to imperialist powers; seeks to end unequal relations.

defeat-communism.rationale: The movement is a communist one, seeking a people's democratic republic as step to socialism, so it opposes defeating communism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Socialism socialises the means of production, and the program protects personal and patriotic private property.

religion-illusion.rationale: Though Marxist and secular in culture, the program guarantees religious freedom and the movement works with religious sectors, so it does not push this thesis.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist tradition credits capitalism historically, but in the Philippines the program treats it as stunted under imperialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The women's emancipation point is part of the full national democratic program.

socialized-care.rationale: The program mentions a progressive social policy and women's emancipation, but no public provision of housework or childcare, so it is neutral.

purge-loanwords.rationale: A national language is promoted without stated purism.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperatives are part of the program but not small self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Supports minority land claims, opposes settler displacement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The movement is explicitly Marxist-Leninist-Maoist, aiming at socialism and communism after a democratic stage, so a third course is rejected.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Nothing in the movement's texts doubts the Holocaust, and denial would run against its anti-fascist stance.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Opposes criminalisation as inconsistent with democratic rights.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Promises democratic rights and a coalition government though it excludes counter-revolutionaries.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 1968 program guarantees freedom of thought, belief and religion, which rules out punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Philippines is analysed as a semi-colony exploited by US interests, and the movement fights this relationship, so it rejects colonies serving the metropole.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not part of its secular doctrine, though it supports the Moro struggle for self-determination.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The program is secular, and its justification for overthrow is class and national oppression, not religious legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The mass line and mass organisations in the national democratic movement emphasise participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class and national oppression are central; women's emancipation is a plank, though not an intersectional framework.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: It places itself on the left against reactionary classes.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The program guarantees religious freedom but does not mention dress in state institutions, so it is neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: It wants a planned economy with state, cooperative and private sectors rather than a market with protections.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The NDFP program builds a people's revolutionary army and a broader people's defence system, so it does not call for abolition of armed forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Calls for an independent foreign policy, but the 1968 program leaned toward China and Albania.

rich-first.rationale: Opposes unequal wealth concentration and prioritises land redistribution.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The program attacks the feudal and dynastic landlord-comprador politics, and aims at a people's democratic republic.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Opposes imperialist financial dominance and unequal relations.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The program calls for women's emancipation and agricultural sustainability but does not link the two as ecofeminism does.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement attacks the landlord and comprador classes that dominate the state and favours wide democratic rights, so wealth tests for voting are opposed.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Sison describes mass media as tools of ruling classes, and the program proposes state control.

racial-franchise.rationale: The program defends democratic rights and the rights of national minorities, which excludes a racial limit on voting.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The movement defends minorities' rights and national unity, so it opposes boycotts aimed at one religious minority.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Concentrated landlord and comprador wealth is seen as the base of ruling-class domination.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The 1968 program guarantees freedom of religion, so active state promotion of atheism is not part of it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: It will keep people's courts and security under the new state.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Coalition government and minority autonomy are in the program.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Structural reform and state social policy are preferred over charity.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Revolutionary bodies stress cadres living simply and serving the masses, but the program sets no pay rule for representatives.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Marxist-Maoist view that social being and class position shape consciousness, with ideas formed through social practice, points to circumstances over innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The program sets up elected representative bodies and condemns feudal and dictatorial rule such as Marcos's.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The program wants rule by the working class-led people, with a coalition of classes, not a balance of few and many.

job-guarantee.rationale: Rural and national industrialisation with rising employment are program points, and the state sector would lead.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist analysis of exploitation is central, though the sources stress exploitation by landlords and compradors rather than alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The program defends the Moro people's self-determination and rights, and condemns Christian chauvinism against Muslims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The program rests authority on the people's democratic revolution under a scientific, secular outlook.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Ending US domination, including its military presence, is central to the national-democratic line and the programme's independent foreign policy.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: A Marxist programme that ends landlord rent and comprador profit through land reform and a state-led economy, so income should follow labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The programme makes protracted people's war its first point, so armed force in defence of the people is fully justified.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The movement commemorates its fallen as revolutionary martyrs, but in a secular sense; the sources do not speak of sainthood.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: A materialist doctrine that sees politics as class struggle and rejects idealist explanations.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The doctrine calls for working-class leadership through the Communist Party in a people's democratic revolution, with socialism as a later stage.

municipal-property.rationale: The program envisages state and cooperative ownership of key industries and land reform for peasants, not municipal ownership.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The doctrine organises by class and nation, not by race.

free-public-college.rationale: The program calls for a national, scientific and mass culture and education serving the people, and the NDFP program promises free education under the people's democratic state.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The movement fights a people's war with its own army against the state, and the 1968 program endorses armed struggle.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The program demands an independent foreign policy and an end to imperialist domination of the economy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Philippine Society and Revolution calls for overthrowing the semi-colonial state through people's war and building new organs of power.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The sources show no ecological pricing; the program treats natural resources as national patrimony to be controlled.

sacred-nation.rationale: Doctrine is class-based, secular and materialist, and treats the colonial church as an instrument of control.

farm-price-support.rationale: Philippine Society and Revolution attacks landlord usury and calls for genuine land reform with cooperatives and state support for peasants.

workers-own-party.rationale: The CPP is described as the party of the proletariat leading the revolution, independent of the established parties it calls reactionary.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 12-point programme promises women equal rights with men, and its land reform aims to give land to the tillers.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1968 program guarantees freedom of religion and separation of church and state, and the movement attacks the colonial church.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Philippine Society and Revolution rejects the existing elections as a sham of the ruling classes; democracy is judged by class content and people's rule.

women-suffrage.rationale: The NDFP program calls for equal rights for women and an end to discrimination, including political participation.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about national or state-level self-government or equality in general, not Indigenous self-government, and the statement now asks whether new Indigenous self-government arrangements should guarantee women's equal participation.

reviewHistory.rationale: The NDFP 12-point program commits to advancing the revolutionary emancipation of women in all spheres, so gender equality in any self-rule arrangement follows from it.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about national or state-level self-government or equality in general, not Indigenous self-government, and the statement now asks whether new Indigenous self-government arrangements should guarantee women's equal participation.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The NDFP program upholds the rights to self-determination and democracy of the Moro people, Cordillera peoples and other national minorities.

close-ties-china.rationale: Maoist origins give sympathy for China, but the programme demands an independent foreign policy against all great powers.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The programme promises free education, health and social services to the people as a whole under the people's democratic state.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The movement rests on the Communist Party leading a coalition of organisations, so organised parties and groups are the link to the people.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The programme guarantees religious freedom and criticises the colonial church's political role; no stated rule on denominational parties.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The programme promotes national culture and science and technology for industrialisation but never frames them as ancestral values.

national-resource-control.rationale: The 12-point programme calls for national industrialisation and ending foreign monopoly control of the economy and resources.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Philippine Society and Revolution applies Marxist political economy, which holds that the value of goods is created by labour, to Philippine society.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: National democracy joins anti-imperialist patriotism to the cause of workers and peasants; the programme calls for a national and democratic revolution led by the working class.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: A progressive social policy is a program plank, and adherents see welfare cuts as part of imperialist neoliberal policy. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Seeking influence in former imperial territories contradicts the movement's opposition to imperialism and unequal relations among nations. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A country's economy should be freed from domination by foreign monopoly capital, even if this means nationalising foreign-owned firms.
missingStatements.rationale: The program names breaking imperialist and compador dominance of the economy as a central aim (point 7).

missingStatements.text: The people have a right to wage armed struggle against a government they regard as a puppet of a foreign power.
missingStatements.rationale: People's war to overthrow the semi-colonial, semi-feudal system is the first point of the NDFP program.

notes: The NDFP is the front around the CPP; Philippine legal organisations in the movement take part in elections. Sources do not cover LGBT rights, drugs, abortion or the environment, so those answers are inferences marked low.
